title: EBS Volume Types & Instance Store
summary: Pick the right block storage for IOPS, throughput, latency and shared access.
tldr: **gp3** is the default SSD: 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s included at any size, with IOPS and throughput provisioned separately from capacity.

**io2 Block Express** when you need very high IOPS, sub-millisecond latency, 99.999% durability or **Multi-Attach**. **st1** for big sequential throughput, **sc1** for the cheapest cold sequential data.
**Instance store** is the fastest, cheapest local NVMe, but the data is lost when the instance stops or fails. Use it only for scratch, cache or data replicated elsewhere.
Change type, size, IOPS or throughput online with **Elastic Volumes**; the instance's own **EBS bandwidth limit** can still cap performance.

keyFacts.text: Current gp3 maximums: 80,000 IOPS and 2,000 MiB/s per volume, up to 64 TiB. Baseline stays 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s. Older material quotes 16,000 / 1,000.
io2 Block Express maximum per volume, with 4,000 MiB/s, 64 TiB and under 500 µs average latency. Only Nitro-based instances get the full performance.
**gp2** performance is tied to size (bursting to 3,000 IOPS on small volumes, 16,000 max), so it often forces over-provisioned capacity. gp3 removes that link.
io1/io2 **Multi-Attach** attaches one volume to up to 16 Nitro instances in the *same AZ*; the app needs a cluster-aware file system.
Maximum throughput of **st1** and **sc1**. Both are HDD, can't be boot volumes, and suit large sequential I/O only.
**EBS Snapshots Archive** cuts storage cost for snapshots kept 90+ days and rarely restored; restoring takes 24–72 hours. Automate it with **Data Lifecycle Manager**.

traps: Multi-Attach works only on io1/io2 in one AZ and isn't a shared file system. For shared files across AZs use EFS or FSx.
Growing a gp3 volume does **not** raise its throughput; gp3 performance is provisioned separately (size-linked performance was gp2 behaviour).
RAID 0 of more volumes doesn't help when the *instance* EBS bandwidth is the bottleneck.
Instance store data does not survive a stop or hardware failure, so it never meets "data must persist".
The EBS Snapshots Archive tier is cheaper storage, not faster restore; restores take 24–72 hours.
Elastic Volumes can grow a volume but never shrink it; to get smaller, copy the data to a new, smaller volume.
You can't encrypt an existing volume in place. Snapshot it, create an encrypted copy, and swap volumes.
